---
title: "Softmax"
description: "A function that converts a vector of real-valued scores into nonnegative values that sum to one."
term: "Softmax"
letter: "S"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

Softmax turns a list of model scores into a distribution across
alternatives. A larger score receives a larger share, and all output values
sum to one.

## Technical explanation

For logits $z_i$, softmax is
$\mathrm{softmax}(z_i)=e^{z_i}/\sum_j e^{z_j}$. Implementations commonly
subtract the maximum logit for numerical stability. Temperature scaling
changes the sharpness of the distribution without changing score order for
positive temperatures.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Softmax is used in multiclass classifiers, attention weights, and token
generation. Its output is often interpreted probabilistically, but
calibration and task context determine whether those values reflect actual
frequencies.

## How it works

Each logit is exponentiated and normalized by the sum of all exponentials.
For classification, the largest output corresponds to the largest logit.
For attention, softmax-normalized scores act as weights used to combine
value vectors.

## Practical example

A classifier with logits $(2,1,0)$ produces a categorical distribution
after softmax. The values express relative model scores; evaluate
calibration separately if probabilities are used for decisions.

## Common misconceptions

- Softmax outputs sum to one within the chosen class set, but are not
  automatically calibrated.
- Softmax over independent binary labels can be inappropriate; sigmoid
  outputs may better represent independent decisions.
